images.title: Two roads to 3/5
images.purpose: Show that small divisions (÷ 2, ÷ 2, ÷ 3) and one division by the biggest common factor 12 both take 36/60 to the same lowest terms, 3/5.
images.composition: Two large fraction cards at the left and right ends with wide space between them, joined by an upper path of three small hops and a lower straight arrow.
images.exact_structure: Left: one large card showing 36/60, outlined teal #0072B2. Right: one large card showing 3/5, outlined reddish purple #CC79A7. Upper path: 3 small curved hop arrows in amber #E69F00, one after another, from the left card to the right card, with one caption above the hops. Lower path: 1 long straight grey #6B7280 arrow from the left card to the right card, with its caption below. A short note centred at the bottom. Exactly 2 cards, 3 hop arrows, 1 straight arrow.

images.takeaway: Small steps or one step by the biggest common factor both give 36/60 = 3/5.
images.description: 36/60 on the left and 3/5 on the right, joined above by three hops marked ÷2, ÷2, ÷3 and below by one arrow marked ÷12; both reach the same lowest terms.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to multiply 2 × 2 × 3 and say why the one big step ÷12 lands on the same card.

image_decisions.why: Two paths to the same lowest terms is a picture idea; one image of the two roads carries it.
